chunks: Look into the affairs of your executives, appoint them after testing, and do not appoint them due to partiality or favoritism, for these two are sources of injustice and treachery.

And select from among them those who are people of experience and modesty, from virtuous families, with early precedence in Islam, for they are the most noble in character, the soundest in honor, the least inclined towards greed, and the most profound in viewing the outcomes of matters.
ai.seo_question: What are the criteria for appointing government officials according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this foundational text of Shia political jurisprudence, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes a rigorous meritocratic framework for governance, warning that appointments based on favoritism (muhabaha) or greed (athara) are root causes of injustice. He prioritizes candidates with proven experience, modesty, and noble lineage, arguing that such individuals possess superior moral character and strategic foresight, thereby ensuring administrative integrity and effective statecraft.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Thereafter, look into the affairs of your executives. Give them appointment after tests and do not appoint them according to partiality or favouritism, because these two things constitute sources of injustice and unfairness.

Select from among them those who are people of experience and modesty, hailing from virtuous houses, having been previously in Islam, because such persons possess high manners and untarnished honour. They are the least inclined towards greed and always have their eyes on the ends of matters.
